title: Changing conservative weightings in bipartite graphs

statement.text: Let ''G=(A,B;E)'' be a bipartite graph, and <math>w:E \to \{1,-1\}</math> a [[conservative weighting]]. Can we determine in polynomial time the maximum number of positive edges that can be negated so that the weighting remains conservative?
